question: Why does Giulia Enders say squatting suits the gut better than sitting on a toilet?
answer: Because of a muscle, the puborectalis, which loops round the end of the gut and kinks it to help keep us continent. Sitting relaxes it only partly, so the kink remains; squatting straightens the passage. Enders notes that much of the world squats, and a footstool brings a sitter closer to that angle.
move: Posture changes how the body's plumbing works, not only how it looks.
simply: A muscle wraps round the end of your gut like a hand bending a hose. Squatting lets go of the bend; sitting only half does.
why: A small footstool in the bathroom is a cheap, harmless change many people find helps, and a reminder that the body was shaped long before chairs.
reference: Giulia Enders, Gut: The Inside Story of Our Body's Most Underrated Organ (Greystone Books, 2015), ch. 1
